title: Toasted Walnut and Brown Sugar Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Walnut-steeped cream sweetened with brown sugar; toasted walnuts folded in.
summary: Following the classic custard method, this version steeps the cream with toasted walnuts and sweetens it with brown sugar, then folds in more toasted walnuts for crunch.

ingredients.note: 100 g for steeping, 80 g for folding in

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the walnuts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 170 °C (150 °C fan) and roast the walnuts on the tray for 8-10 min until fragrant and a shade darker. Cool and chop; toasting deepens their flavour and softens any bitterness in the skins.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Bring the cream and milk to steaming, add 100 g of the walnuts, cover and leave for 1 h. Sieve, pressing hard, and discard the soaked nuts, which have given up their flavour.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with the brown sugar and salt in the heatproof bowl until smooth.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Rewarm the walnut cream until steaming and whisk it gradually into the yolks, then return to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat until it coats the spatula and reaches 77-80 °C. Brown sugar makes the custard look darker, so use the thermometer rather than colour.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Add the vanilla, sieve, cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and fold
steps.text: Churn until thick, then fold in the remaining 80 g of chopped walnuts by hand.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h before serving.

tips: Watch the walnuts in the oven: they go from toasted to burnt in a minute.
A common mistake is skipping the pressing step, which leaves flavour behind in the nuts; press firmly with a ladle.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
